title: LECTURE 07 — Design Specifications: Layout, Spacing, Air
text: LECTURE 07 Design Specifications: Layout, Spacing, Air Movement & Enclosure The design-answer chapter: always draw 1. Design specification checklist The lecture organizes climate-responsive design around five practical controls: Layout, Spacing, Air movement, Enclosure and Shading Device. Shortcut L-S-A-E-S = Layout - Spacing - Air movement - Enclosure - Shading. মনে রাখো: “লেআউট-স্পেস-বাতাস- খোলস-ছায়া”. 2. Layout for wind and climate  Broad spacing can improve breeze penetration in warm-humid climates.  Staggered layout often avoids wind shadows and improves airflow through a group of buildings.  Building orientation can be adjusted about 30-45 degrees to wind direction where suitable to improve exposure and flow distribution.  In hot-dry/composite cases, compactness may reduce exposed surface area and unwanted heat gain; design must respond to season and climate type. 3. Spacing and functional distribution  Organize functions according to heat, privacy, day/night use and air movement.  Use floor height and internal voids/courtyards to support air movement and thermal stratification.  Separate served and service zones where this helps buffer unwanted heat. P/A ratio For a given floor area, a compact form generally has a lower perimeter-to-area (P/A) ratio, which reduces exposed envelope area. Circular/compact geometries have low P/A ratios, while highly articulated forms have higher exposure. 4. Air movement and openings Page Page

title: LECTURE 09 — Shading Devices & Effective Shading
text: LECTURE 09 Shading Devices & Effective Shading Solar control with orientation-sensitive sketches 1. Why shading? The principal purpose of sun shading is to prevent unwanted solar radiation when external conditions are above comfort level. Shading can also help control glare, rain exposure, privacy/visibility and sometimes wind direction. Solar path into building Meaning Direct radiation Beam radiation directly through an opening. Reflected radiation Solar radiation reflected from ground/adjacent surfaces. Scattered sky radiation, important in cloudy/warm-humid Diffuse radiation conditions. Solar heat absorbed by roof/wall and later conducted/radiated Indirect through opaque surface inward. 2. External vs internal shading External shading is generally more effective for heat control because it stops solar radiation before it passes through the glazing and becomes indoor heat. Internal curtains can control glare but the absorbed solar heat is already inside the envelope. 3. Types Basic types: horizontal, vertical and combined shading. title: LECTURE 01 — Climatic Study & Bioclimatic Architecture
text: LECTURE 01 — Climatic Study & Bioclimatic Architecture 1. Climatic Design কেন দরকার? Climatic design হলো এমন design approach যেখানে building-কে স্থানীয় climate-এর সাথে “fit” করানো হয়, যাতে comfort পাওয়া যায় এবং mechanical energy demand কমে। Lecture slide-এর মূল কথা: “Building must be designed to fit in with their climate.” Climatic study কী সাহায্য করে Design implication Comfortable indoor climate temperature, airflow, solar exposure নিয়ন্ত্রণ Energy-saving structural design passive control আগে; mechanical system পরে Protection from external factors sun, wind, rain, humidity অনুযায়ী envelope Natural resource utilisation sunlight, breeze, vegetation, site features ব্যবহার Regional architectural character ভিন্ন climate → ভিন্ন form, opening, material, method Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — C-E-P-N Comfort → Energy saving → Protection → Natural resources. Climatic study-এর benefits এই ৪ শব্দে মনে রাখো। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2016 10 Importance of climate study for a BECM graduate. 2017 15 Where can a BECM professional use learning from Climate & Architectural Design? 2. কেন building form এক জায়গা থেকে আরেক জায়গায় বদলায়?  Climate condition building arrangement/design-কে প্রভাবিত করে।  Requirement determination (কী পরিমাণ shade/ventilation/thermal protection দরকার) climate নির্ভ র।  Equipment selection climate-load-এর সাথে সম্পর্কি ত।  Building method, material এবং formation regional climate-এর প্রতিক্রিয়া। Core idea Same function ≠ same building. Climate বদলালে form, envelope, opening, roof, material এবং orientation বদলাতে পারে। 3. Bioclimatic Architecture Bioclimatic বলতে lecture slide-এ “relationship between living organisms and architecture” বোঝানো হয়েছে। অর্থাৎ nature/environment-এর logic ব্যবহার করে building form ও performance optimize করা।  Nature-inspired response, কিন্তু শুধুই aesthetic imitation নয়।  Sun, wind, terrain, vegetation ও seasonal conditionকে design input হিসেবে নেয়।  Goal: comfort + lower energy demand + better environmental fit. title: LECTURE 02 — Global Climatic Factors
text: LECTURE 02 — Global Climatic Factors 1. Climate vs Weather Term Meaning Time scale Climate একটি স্থানের দীর্ঘ সময়ের weather প্রায় 20-30 years pattern Weather নির্দি ষ্ট সময় ও স্থানের atmospheric day-to-day / short term condition Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — Weather = Today, Climate = Trend আজ কী হচ্ছে = weather; দীর্ঘমেয়াদে সাধারণত কী হয় = climate। 2. Latitude, Altitude & Land-Water Relationship  Latitude = Equator-এর উত্তর/দক্ষিণে angular distance. Low latitude বেশি solar exposure পায়; high latitude তু লনামূলক ঠান্ডা।  Altitude = mean sea level-এর ওপরে উচ্চতা. Lecture slide: air rises becomes cooler; তাই পাহাড়ের ওপর নিচের তু লনায় ঠান্ডা।  Large water body climate moderate করে, কারণ land-এর তু লনায় water ধীরে heat up/cool down করে।  Tropical environment roughly 23.5°N থেকে 23.5°S; lecture slide-এ rainforest, monsoon, savanna climate উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2018 15 Why is it always colder at higher altitudes? title: 7. Radiation at the Earth's Surface
text: 7. Radiation at the Earth's Surface Surface-এ পৌঁছানো radiation তিনটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ কারণে বদলায়: angle of incidence, atmospheric depletion এবং sunshine duration. 7.1 Cosine Law If radiation is oblique, same energy spreads over a larger area; intensity falls. I_tilted = I_normal × cos β β = angle between solar ray and the normal to the surface  Normal incidence energy concentrated intensity maximum.  Oblique incidence → same radiation larger area-তে spread intensity কম। 7.2 Atmospheric Depletion Atmosphere-এর ozone, vapour, dust ইত্যাদি radiation absorb/scatter করে; ফলে surface-এ energy কমে। 7.3 Duration of Sunshine Daylight/sunshine কতক্ষণ পাওয়া যাচ্ছে সেটি total solar receipt-কে প্রভাবিত করে। Duration আর intensity একই জিনিস নয়—এই distinction পরে Elements of Climate-এ আবার আসবে। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2023 10 Evaluate Radiation of the Earth's Surface from global climate variation viewpoint. 2024 9 Evaluate Radiation of the Earth's Surface from viewpoint of climate variation at global scale.

title: 9. Global Wind Pattern — mechanism
text: 9. Global Wind Pattern — mechanism Pressure belts and prevailing surface winds  Equator বেশি heat পায় → surface air warm, expands, becomes light rises equatorial low pressure.  Rising warm-humid air upper level-এ subtropical zone-এর দিকে যায়; cooling/densification-এর পর ~30° latitude- এ sink করে → subtropical high.  Subtropical high থেকে এক branch equator-এ ফেরে (trade wind), অন্য branch subpolar front-এর দিকে যায় (westerlies).  Polar region cold/dense polar high; surface flow subpolar low-এর দিকে → polar easterlies.  এভাবে Hadley, Ferrel, Polar circulation cells ও pressure belts তৈরি হয়। Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — 0-30-60-90 0° = low (ITCZ), 30° = high, 60° = low, 90° = high. Pressure-belt sequence মনে রাখলে wind pattern সহজ হয়। 10. Humidity — AH, RH & Vapour Pressure Term Definition / formula Unit Absolute Humidity (AH) Actual moisture present per unit g/kg or g/m³ mass/volume of air. Relative Humidity (RH) Actual moisture / moisture-holding % capacity at same temperature × 100 Vapour pressure (Pv) Partial pressure due to water vapour in N/m² air. title: LECTURE 03.1 — Elements for Building Designers
text: LECTURE 03.1 — Elements for Building Designers 1. Driving Rain & Driving Rain Index (DRI) Driving rain = wind-driven rain যা verticalভাবে না পড়ে angle-এ building envelope-এ আঘাত করে এবং joints, window reveals, cracks/gaps দিয়ে water penetration ঘটাতে পারে। Driving rain mechanism and DRI thresholds DRI = Annual Rainfall (m) × Annual Average Wind Speed (m/s) Unit in the lecture: m²/s Exposure DRI Design meaning Sheltered m 3² / s Low combined wind-rain exposure; normal detailing Moderate 3-7 m²/s More careful joints, sills, reveals and weatherproofing Severe > 7 m²/s Highly exposed/coastal/hilltop; robust envelope and gap control Worked example from slide Annual rainfall 1.2 m × average wind 4.0 m/s = DRI 4.8 m²/s → Moderate exposure. Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — R × V DRI মনে রাখো: Rainfall × Velocity. বেশি rain বা বেশি wind—দুটিই exposure বাড়ায়। Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2021 5 Short note: Driving Rain. 2022 10 Define driving rain. Sky Condition & Cloud Cover  Sky condition mainly cloud presence/absence দিয়ে described হয়.  Typical observation around 09:00 and 15:00; night records comparatively limited.  Cloud cover tenths/eighths (octas) বা percentage-এ expressed হতে পারে: 50% = 5/10 = 4/8.  Designer-এর observation time/frequency জানা দরকার, কারণ sky condition diffuse radiation ও daylight influence করে. 3. Solar Radiation — Sunshine Duration vs Radiation Intensity Item Sunshine Duration Radiation Intensity Meaning How long bright sun shines Actual radiant power per unit area Typical unit hours/day, monthly average W/m²; also Btu/ft²·h, kcal/m²·h Instrument Sunshine recorder (Campbell-Stokes type) Pyranometer / pyrheliometer / actinometer / solarimeter Design use Long-term sunshine availability Directly relates to solar heat gain Very important distinction Zero bright-sunshine hours does NOT mean zero solar energy: an overcast sky can still deliver diffuse radiation. 4. text: LECTURE 05 — Regional, Site & Urban Climate 1. Macroclimate, Site Climate & Microclimate Regional data is the starting point; local modifiers create site-specific deviation . Scale Meaning Regional / macroclimate Broad climate described by regional/met station data. Site climate Climate of the actual area available for the project, horizontally and vertically. Microclimate Very local climate around a building/space; scale depends on discipline. Important Macroclimate is useful as a guide, but lecture says it is seldom sufficient in accuracy for a particular site. 2. How to assess site climate for a large site 6. title: 3. Factors Constituting Regional Climate
text: 3. Factors Constituting Regional Climate Level Factors Primary Global climatic factors; detailed slide highlights temperature, humidity, air flow as primary climatic outcomes. Secondary Location of region; diurnal variation; altitude. Tertiary Soil condition; topography; natural wind breakers; man-made wind breakers; water bodies; cities/industries; deserts. Local & minor Ocean current; sky condition; smog; smoke; fog; thunder/lightning; sand storms. Shortcut / মনে রাখার কৌশল — P-S-T-L Primary → Secondary → Tertiary → Local. প্রথমে hierarchy লিখলে বড় প্রশ্নের structure নিজে থেকেই তৈরি হয়। 4. Key local modifiers — quick explanations Factor Effect Soil condition Stony/sandy surface quickly heats and reradiates; fine/organic soil behaves differently. Topography Cool heavy air settles in depressions → locally cooler/humid conditions. Natural wind breaker Mountains/large trees obstruct or redirect wind. Ocean current Warm/cool currents transport heat and modify coastal temperature/humidity/rainfall. Smog / smoke / fog Modify humidity, radiation, visibility and air quality. Sand storm Openings/ventilators require protection; façade treatment may respond to dust/sand. title: 6. Urban Climate
text: 6. Urban Climate  Changed surface qualities: pavements/buildings absorb more solar energy ; evaporation decreases .  Buildings cast shadows, block/channel wind, store heat and release it slowly.  Energy seepage: AC/refrigeration, electrical appliances, engines and industry add heat .  Atmospheric pollution forms a barrier to outgoing radiation. title: LECTURE 06 — Thermal Comfort & Human Heat Balance
text: LECTURE 06 — Thermal Comfort & Human Heat Balance 1. Why Thermal Comfort matters  Daily life cycle = activity fatigue recovery ; unfavorable climate এই cycle disturb করতে পারে.  Thermal stress discomfort, reduced efficiency এবং health breakdown ঘটাতে পারে.  Therefore building designer must understand both climate and how the human body acts/reacts to heat . Definition idea Thermal comfort = এমন thermal condition যেখানে মানুষের body heat balance বজায় থাকে এবং ব্যক্তি পরিবেশকে thermally acceptable মনে করে. Lecture emphasis is on physiological balance and comfort variables. Question Bank Match — পরীক্ষায় যেভাবে এসেছে নিচের wording পাঠযোগ্য করার জন্য সামান্য normalised করা হয়েছে; বছর ও marks স্ক্যানে যতটা স্পষ্ট, ততটাই রাখা হয়েছে। Year Marks Matching question / focus 2023 10 Describe significance of thermal comfort for human body. 2024 12 What is thermal comfort? How does the human body maintain thermal balance? 2. Metabolism & Heat Production  Metabolism = foodকে living matter ও energy-তে convert করার process.  Basal metabolism = continuous automatic/vegetative process.  Muscular metabolism = consciously controlled muscular work.  Lecture slide states roughly 20% produced heat is used inside body and remaining 80% surplus heat must be dissipated. Activity Heat production (W) — lecture table Sleeping Min. 70 Sitting / typing / light bench work 130-160 Sitting, heavy arm/leg movements 190-230 Standing moderate work / some walking 220-290 Walking + moderate lifting/pushing 290-410 Intermittent heavy lifting/digging 440-580 Hardest sustained work 580-700 Maximum heavy work ~30 min Max. 1100 Source-note Billah Sir class note marks the heat-production table as “not need to memorize”; understand the trend: more activity → higher metabolic heat.

title: 3. Human Heat Gain & Heat Loss
text: 3. Human Heat Gain & Heat Loss Redrawn heat-exchange sketch: conduction, convection, radiation , evaporation Mode Heat gain / loss logic Metabolism Internal heat production. Conduction Direct contact; depends on surface temperature difference. Convection Heat exchange with air touching skin/clothing; faster air movement usually increases convective exchange. Radiation Heat exchange with surrounding surfaces / sun without direct contact. Evaporation Sweat + imperceptible perspiration + breathing; dry air allows faster evaporation. text: How to Use This Analysis The 3-out-of-4 Reality The safest strategy is not to memorize isolated questions. Each main question often mixes 2-4 subtopics. Climatic Comfort Indices Effective Temperature (ET)  Different air-temperature + humidity combinations can feel equally comfortable.  ET scale combines Temperature + Humidity + Air movement on a psychrometric basis.  Radiation effect is not included in basic ET. Corrected Effective Temperature (CET)  ET scale is corrected by incorporating radiation effect.  Hence CET is more complete than ET where radiant environment matters. Equivalent Warmth (EW) & Operative Temperature (OT)  EW correlates air temperature, humidity, mean radiant temperature with skin/clothing surface temperature.  OT combines effects of radiation and air temperature; humidity and air movement are treated as negligible in the lecture slide. Shortcut - ET-CET ET = T + H + Air movement. CET = ET + Radiation. Condition Response Thermal effect More warm blood reaches skin → skin temperature rises → greater Warm / overheating Vasodilation: skin blood vessels widen. convective/radiant loss; sweating may follow. Less warm blood reaches skin → skin Vasoconstriction: skin blood vessels Cold / underheating temperature falls → heat loss slows; narrow. shivering may follow. Vasodilation vs vasoconstriction - redraw as a simple flow diagram. Design implication  Avoid prolonged indoor conditions that force continuous sweating or shivering .  Use air speed to aid evaporation in warm conditions, but avoid excessive cold drafts.  Reduce radiant heat from roofs/walls so vasodilation does not have to compensate for large radiant gains .  Allow adaptive variation rather than a perfectly fixed condition all day.

Atmospheric depletion; why 2022 6(b) 10 colder at higher altitude? 2023 5(c) 5 Illustrate atmospheric depletion. Atmospheric depletion is the reduction of solar radiation as it passes through the atmosphere by absorption and scattering by ozone, water vapour, dust, clouds and other particles. A longer atmospheric path generally causes greater depletion. Incidence and atmospheric path are separate effects on received solar energy. Higher altitude - exam-safe explanation The lecture states that rising air becomes cooler. At lower pressure aloft , ascending air expands and cools , so average air temperature generally decreases with elevation. The atmosphere is also heated strongly from the ground upward , so being closer to the sun is not the controlling effect.

Working mechanism of rat-trap 2023 8(c) 8 bond. Rat-trap bond is a brick masonry technique in which bricks are placed on edge/vertical orientation so that a continuous cavity is formed within the wall thickness. The cavity reduces material use and improves thermal and acoustic resistance when the wall is properly detailed. Rat-trap bond - cavity formed within a nominal brick-wall thickness. Construction rules  Use consistent good-quality bricks; dimensional variation affects the bond.  Keep bottom/top closure courses and opening jamb/sill/lintel zones solid where required .  Maintain the cavity without excessive mortar droppings bridging it.  Provide reinforcement/bands/corner detailing where structural design or seismic requirements demand it .  Plan services carefully so the cavity is not unintentionally destroyed. Advantages  Lower brick and mortar use; the lecture slide reports approximately 25% fewer bricks and 40% less mortar than conventional masonry in one comparison.  Cavity improves thermal insulation: cooler inside in summer, warmer in winter.  Lower material demand can reduce cost and embodied impact.  Exposed brickwork can reduce plaster where workmanship is good. Structural caution The slide says strength is not compromised. Exam-safe wording: properly designed and constructed rat-trap masonry can provide adequate wall performance; actual structural capacity depends on materials, workmanship, reinforcement/detailing and code requirements.

title: Coriolis directions
text: Coriolis directions  Northern Hemisphere: moving air deflects to the right.  Southern Hemisphere: moving air deflects to the left.  Therefore trades are easterly, mid-latitude winds are westerly and polar surface winds are easterly.

title: B1.5 ITCZ / Doldrums and Annual Wind Shift
text: B1.5 ITCZ / Doldrums and Annual Wind Shift Priority: S - very high | Asked: 2016, 2021, 2023, 2024 | Marks: 10-15 Year Q. Marks Question focus Impact of annual wind shift from 2016 3(b) 15 north to south of equator. Relationship between ITCZ and 2021 1(b) 10 annual wind shifts. Doldrums: location and 2023 2(b) 10 formation. Why ITCZ is calm and why it shifts 2024 1(b) 12 more toward Northern Hemisphere. Seasonal migration of the ITCZ - conceptual annual shift around the equator. The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is the equatorial/sub-equatorial belt where the NE and SE trade winds converge. Warm moist air rises, so surface horizontal wind can be weak, variable and calm - the traditional “doldrums”. Why it shifts  The zone of maximum solar heating migrates north and south with the apparent seasonal movement of the sun .  ITCZ follows this thermal low, moving northward in northern summer and southward in northern winter .  It often migrates farther north over the Northern Hemisphere because there is more land , and land heats more strongly/quickly than ocean in summer, pulling the thermal low northward. Effects of the annual shift  Seasonal reversal/shift of prevailing winds.  Monsoon circulation and seasonal rainfall migration.  Changes in cloud, humidity and storm activity.  Important seasonal design changes in ventilation and rain protection.

title: B1.6 Earth-Sun Relationship, tilt of axis and seasonal solar distribution

How tilt affects solar radiation 2024 1(a) 8 distribution and seasons. Earth-Sun geometry: solstices, equinoxes and axial tilt.  Earth axis is about 23.5° from the perpendicular to the orbital plane (equivalent to 66.5° to the orbital plane in the lecture wording).  Because the tilted Earth revolves around the Sun, solar angle and day length change by latitude and season .  Around 21 June the overhead-sun zone reaches the Tropic of Cancer; around 21 December it reaches the Tropic of Capricorn.  Around 21 March and 23 September, solar declination is near the equator (equinox).  Higher sun angle concentrates radiation; lower angle spreads energy over larger area and increases atmospheric path.

title: B1.7 Influence of Topography on climate variation
text: B1.7 Influence of Topography on climate variation Priority: A - repeated | Asked: 2021, 2023, 2024/related | Marks: 5-10 Year Q. Marks Question focus Influence of topography on global 2021 1(a) 10 climate variations. Topographical factors responsible 2023 4(a) 5 for global climate variation. Local site deviations also depend 2024 3(a) related on topography.  Altitude: temperature generally decreases with height; mountain climates differ from valleys .  Slope/aspect: changes solar exposure and therefore surface heating.  Orographic effect: mountains force moist air upward, supporting cloud/rain on windward sides and drier conditions in rain-shadow zones.  Cold-air drainage: dense cool air can settle in depressions/valleys and produce local inversions .  Wind modification: hills, ridges and valleys block, accelerate, channel or create turbulence in airflow . Conclusion Topography does not create the global circulation by itself; it modifies the general climate into distinct regional and site climates.

How desert forms in subtropical 2024 2(c) 12 region and why day-night range is large. 2021: protective measures in warm-humid climate  Provide maximum ventilation and air movement with large, well-positioned openings.  Provide maximum shading against both direct and diffuse solar radiation.  Avoid unnecessary heat storage; favour light construction where appropriate.  Use reflective/light-coloured outer surfaces and well-insulated, ventilated double roofs .  Use vegetation for shade and microclimate moderation without blocking useful breezes .  Protect walls/openings from heavy rain and moisture while keeping airflow paths open. Standard meteorological meaning: a temperature inversion occurs when temperature increases with height over a layer instead of normally decreasing. Cool dense air can be trapped near the ground beneath warmer air. Typical causes / example  Night-time radiative cooling of ground under clear calm conditions can cool the near-surface air.  Cold air can drain into valleys/depressions and become trapped.  A warm layer above suppresses vertical mixing, allowing fog/smog and pollutants to accumulate . Exam caution Do not claim “global warming causes all inversions”. title: B4.7 Atmospheric Pressure
text: B4.7 Atmospheric Pressure Priority: B - short repeated | Asked: 2022, 2023 | Marks: 5 Year Q. Marks Question focus Briefly describe atmospheric 2022 3(a) 5 pressure. Briefly describe atmospheric 2023 2(d) 5 pressure. Atmospheric pressure is the force per unit area exerted by the weight of the air column above a surface . In moist air it can be considered as the sum of the partial pressure of dry air and the partial pressure of water vapour . P = P_a + P_v P_a = partial pressure of dry air; P_v = vapour pressure.  Pressure generally decreases with altitude.  Pressure differences drive wind from higher toward lower pressure, then Coriolis and friction modify direction .  Heating can make air less dense and contribute to rising motion/low-pressure development.
